_comment: The labelled query set, one per test pack. Labels reference (source_uid, stable_key)
and never chunk_id: a pack-local id does not survive a rebuild of the corpus, and a
label set that silently re-points at different passages after a fixture change is
worse than no label set -- it keeps reporting a recall number for the wrong
questions. Same reason supersession targets a stable key.
Negative queries carry an empty 'relevant' list and assert the refusal. They are as
important as the positive ones: the refusal is the visible half of the
refuse-rather-than-hallucinate rule, and a retrieval change that quietly starts
answering them is exactly the regression that would otherwise ship.

The threshold is a mean over every query, positives and negatives alike. It is not 1.0 because one positive is a known miss (see its notes); every negative must still refuse, which the harness asserts separately and absolutely rather than folding into the mean. A refusal that quietly becomes an answer is the regression this set exists to catch, and an average is the wrong instrument for catching it.

TWO THRESHOLDS, because there are two tiers. 'structural_threshold' is what the deterministic stand-in embedder must meet on every PR: it measures that the pipeline works, not that the embeddings are good. 'threshold' is the semantic tier's gate, run when a real embedder contract is bundled. Queries needing genuine semantic bridging -- GM-facing phrasings that share almost no vocabulary with the passage -- are expected to miss structurally and to pass semantically. Keeping one number for both would either make the per-PR gate untrue or make the semantic gate meaningless.

queries.notes: table slang; the book calls it seizing and never says grapple

queries.query: what happens when I grab a creature and win

queries.notes: KNOWN MISS on this corpus. Scores 0.278 on the information gate, just under the 0.283 of the 'warhorse' negative, because across twenty chunks the word 'mean' occurs nowhere and so counts as unmatched information exactly as 'warhorse' does. The threshold is set above both, which loses this question and holds every refusal. On a real SRD 'mean' appears throughout and the overlap disappears.

queries.query: how do I put out a fire on someone who is burning
how many points do I get for aptitudes
how much harm can a character take

queries.notes: the Bright Success rule, asked without its name

queries.query: what lives in the cinder marches
queries.notes: route 3: lore, answered generatively over redacted text

queries.query: what do travellers say about the mountain
queries.notes: The rumour table is nested inside the Marches lore, so the lore chunk genuinely answers this and is what nesting dedup surfaces when the parent matches independently. Labelling only the child would be asserting a dedup outcome the spec does not call for.

queries.query: does heavy ashfall make it harder to see
why is nothing alive on the old road
what do the players hear at the start of the ascent
queries.notes: SEMANTIC TIER. A GM-facing phrasing sharing almost no vocabulary with the boxed text it asks about -- 'hear' and 'players' occur nowhere in it. Nothing lexical can bridge that and no surface-overlap stand-in can either, which is the whole reason the dense half of the pipeline exists.
